title: Backyard Seismograph Quake Detection
dataSources: Seismograph (`seismo:reading`), Geiger counter (`geiger:cpm`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), radon (`radon:reading`), all-sky meteor camera (`allsky:capture`), river-level gauge (`riverlevel:reading`), magnetometer (`magnetometer:reading`).
app: DIY citizen-science sensors — Raspberry Shake seismograph, DIY Geiger counter, AS3935/Blitzortung lightning detector, radon monitor, all-sky meteor camera, river-level gauge, and magnetometer — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading
| eventstats avg(amplitude) as base, stdev(amplitude) as sd
| eval quake=if(amplitude>base+6*sd,1,0)
| where quake=1
| table _time amplitude base
description: Flags ground-motion spikes far above your sensor's quiet baseline, catching real earthquakes among the everyday rumble of traffic.
value: A personal seismograph is only useful if it separates a genuine quake from a passing truck; a statistical baseline does exactly that.
implementation: Stream Raspberry Shake amplitude into `index=personal`; alert when motion jumps well above the rolling background level.
visualization: Time chart of ground-motion amplitude with detected quakes marked.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Citizen Science & Backyard Sensing — typical feeds: Seismograph (`seismo:reading`), Geiger counter (`geiger:cpm`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), radon (`radon:reading`), all-sky meteor camera (`allsky:capture`), river-level gauge (`riverlevel.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `seismo:reading`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=seismo:reading`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** DIY citizen-science sensors — Raspberry Shake seismograph, Geiger counter, AS3935/Blitzortung lightning detector, radon monitor, all-sky meteor camera, river-level gauge, and magnetometer — via MQTT and scripted inputs to Splunk HEC..

**Author notes:** Stream Raspberry Shake amplitude into `index=personal`; alert when motion jumps well above the rolling background level.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "seismo:reading", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Backyard Seismograph Quake Detection** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=seismo:reading`) across the full search range. `eventstats` / `streamstats` compute rolling baselines before filtering outliers; window size controls sensitivity (smaller window = noisier alerts).

**Fields this search depends on:** `quake`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading
| eventstats avg(amplitude) as base, stdev(amplitude) as sd
| eval quake=if(amplitude>base+6*sd,1,0)
| where quake=1
| table _time amplitude base
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table quake
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.20.1: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Time Chart Of Ground-Motion Amplitude With Detected Quakes Marked (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `seismo:reading` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Everything is an outlier:** Baseline window is too short or `stdev=0` — require minimum sample count (`where count>=5`) before computing z-scores.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
